To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

patients with primary ciliary dyskenesis (PCD) are at increased risk for congenital heart disease and situs defects, and that patients with PCD who have consanguineous parent have a higher risk for situs defects than patients who have non-consanguineus parents.
patients with PCD and biallelic variants in nine PCD genes were less likely to have situs defects and/or CHD, and patients with consanguineity were more likely to have situr defects and/or CHDs.
patients with bialleic mutations in a subset (9/25) of PCD genes have normal situs and patients with abnormal situs have higher odds of CHO and/or laterality defect than patients with normal situs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a genetic disease called primary ciliary dyskenesia (PCD).
the identification and characterisation of the genetic causes of PCD, and the relationship between the genetic causes of this condition and its clinical manifestations.
the development of a new method for predicting the presence of situs defects and CHD in PCD, which is important in clinical decision-making.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
patients with PCD have a 25% risk for situs abnormalities and a 25% for congenital cardiac defects.
patients with PCD have an increased likelihood of abnormal situs and CHD, and that the risk for these conditions can be predicted by the presence of specific PCD mutations.
the presence of a situs defect is a risk factor for CHD and other laterality defects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

patients with PCD and biallelic variants in a subset of PCD genes do not have situs defects and patients with PCD with consanguineus parents are more likely to have situs defects than patients with PCD without consanguineus parentage.
the risk of situs abnormalities and laterality defects in PCD is increased in the presence of consanguineous matings and in the absence of biallelic disease in the subset of nine genes studied.
patients with PCD and a subset of PCD-causing genes have normal situs, and patients with PCD with abnormal situs have higher odds of CHDs and/or laterality abnormalities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients with bialleic PCD-causing mutations in a subset genes are unlikely to have situs defects.
patients with PCD have an increased risk of situs defects and CHD.
patients with PCD are at risk of cardiac and laterality abnormalities.
